description:
Populate a directory category from the tenant's IDAP data
(norm_cli_*.businesses). norm_cli_* is the canonical store for every
business SpiderIQ has seen for this tenant (SpiderMaps + SpiderSite +
SpiderCompanyData + SpiderPeople merged). This reads directly — no
scheduler, no sync pipeline, no external call.

🔴 THIS IS AN UPSERT KEYED ON (category, slug) — RE-RUNNING IT NEVER REMOVES
ANYTHING. A business deleted from IDAP, or renamed so it produces a different
slug, leaves its old listing PUBLISHED IN THE DIRECTORY FOREVER. Successive
imports only ever add and update, so a category drifts further from its source
on every run. `prune: true` is the fix and it is OFF BY DEFAULT.

`prune: true` ARCHIVES (never deletes — status='archived', which drops the row
out of every published door and is reversible with directory_upsert_listing)
every listing in the category that this import's own result set did not produce.
It refuses rather than guess, and reports the refusal in `prune_skipped_reason`:
  · source_returned_no_rows   — an empty result set is far more often a filter
                                that matched nothing than a category that
                                genuinely emptied; pruning there would archive
                                everything. Confirm the filter returns rows first.
  · source_truncated_at_limit — the SELECT hit `limit`, so the full matching set
                                is unknown and "absent from the page" is a
                                pagination artefact, not a deletion. Raise limit
                                or narrow the filter.
A prune-refusal is an ANSWER, not a transient error: re-running unchanged
refuses identically.

Every column the tenant's businesses table declares is carried through (typed
column where one exists, otherwise into the listing's `data` JSONB) — this is
no longer a hand-picked subset.

URL shape produced: /{directory_base}/{category_slug}/{city_slug}/{listing_slug},
where directory_base is the tenant's per-tenant prefix and defaults to
"directory". city_slug is derived server-side from the imported city + state —
you never pass it. The same listings are also reachable FLAT (no category/city
segments) from a dynamic_list page bound to collection_type "directory_listings".

Filters (all optional): category_filter matches the categories[] array,
country_code exact (uppercase), city is ILIKE substring, rating_min is
inclusive. limit caps at 5000 to align with bulk_upsert.

Returns {upserted, inserted, updated, pruned, failed, source_rows,
affected_cities, source_schema, fields_mapped, filter, sync_log_id,
failures?, prune_skipped_reason?, hint?}. If the tenant has no norm_cli_*
schema yet (never ran SpiderMaps), hint explains the workaround.

project.description: Optional project — a website inside the workspace (proj_xxx) — to scope this call to. Sent as the X-Project-Id header. If omitted, the spideriq.json / SPIDERIQ_PROJECT_ID binding (or the workspace default project) is used.

prune.description: ARCHIVE listings this import did not produce (default false). Without it the import is add/update only and stale listings stay published forever. Refuses on an empty or limit-truncated result set and tells you which, in `prune_skipped_reason`.

workspace.description: Tenant to target (cli_…). Omit to use the active/bound workspace. list_workspaces shows the options.

name: directory_import_from_idap
